title: Health Education & Physical Education Professional Development
before:
The Health Education and Physical Education Program provides professional learning opportunities for teachers in the field to develop their skills and continue learning through events, webinars, and online learning. Links to events and organizations are for reference and information only and do not imply endorsement by the Maine Department of Education.

Upcoming Events

 
Recorded Sessions
  • Naloxone Education in Maine Schools - Train the Trainer a Maine DOE hosted webinar that supports implementation of the revisions to Chapter 41, regarding naloxone education for students.
  • 2021 MIYHS Highlights with Sheila Nelson from Maine CDC
  • Maine DOE Health Education and Physical Education playlists: recorded videos of past webinars and video meetings with relevant HE & PE information from specialists, partners, and fellow educators.
  • Maine DOE YouTube Channel Playlists: recorded videos of webinars and meetings on a wide variety of topics from specialists, partners, and fellow educators.
Other Opportunities
  • 2026 Winter Wellness Summit — visit the 2026 Summit website to access information and resources made available by presenters at the Summit.
  • 2026 Maine AHPERD Annual Conference at The Samoset Resort, November 1-3, 2026.
  • NAMI Maine provides a variety of suicide prevention education and awareness trainings. Visit their calendar for details.
  • SHAPE America offers professional learning opportunities in health education and physical education The 2027 SHAPE America National Convention & Expo will take place in Charlotte, North Carolina, at the Charlotte Convention Center from April 7-10.
Maine Department of Education Professional Learning Resources
  • Interdisciplinary Instruction: open-sourced resources, including a mix of video and text options, that support educator growth. Contact hours are available for the self-paced, professional learning modules.
  • MOOSE: a free, optional resource for PreK-12 educators aligned to the Maine Learning Results. Modules have been created in topic areas and themes, including health education and physical education content.
  • EnGiNE: an online library designed to engage innovation in education. Curriculum resources, professional learning modules, and collaboration tools are available for educators to share and develop creative solutions to 21st-century learning challenges.

notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 5 links on this page open a file — 5 Video — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Give the cards the width their content needs
decisions.why: 1 row holds two cards of very different weight in equal halves, and cards in a row are the same height — so the short one is stretched and the difference shows as empty space. 2.4× — 1572 characters beside 642. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 1 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 8 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Let a colon do its own work
decisions.why: A colon marks the words before it as a term and the words after it as what the term means. 4 links sit immediately in front of a colon, where the chevron lands between the term and the punctuation that belongs to it. 1 format tag stands between a title and its description and moves to the end of the row. No word changes and nothing is removed.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 3 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
